register.name: Regional Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Solutions (Regional DARES), first phase
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 22 June 2026 · with Benin, the Central African Republic and Liberia · first phase of an $853 million programme
register.note: Sierra Leone’s share of the US$200 million first phase (World Bank, Finances One)
register.text: Finances solar home systems, mini-grids and other off-grid renewable technologies for rural, isolated and underserved communities, and power for schools and health centres. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach: 39.2% of Sierra Leoneans have electricity and 2% cook with clean fuels.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 18 June 2026 · SDR 155.55 million, 75% of quota · alongside the Extended Credit Facility
register.note: Disbursements begin on completion of the first review; to be used for budget support
register.text: The IMF’s climate resilience arrangement with Sierra Leone, approved with the third review of the Extended Credit Facility. Its reforms cover public financial management, disaster risk management and social safety nets, adaptation in water and land management, and financial sector risk management, which bear on the water, food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 31 October 2024 · 38 months · third review 18 June 2026 · next disbursement available from 15 November 2026, on the fourth review
register.note: SDR 116.664 million (about US$158.6 million) disbursed after the third review
register.text: The IMF’s main lending programme with Sierra Leone, with access of SDR 186.663 million, 90% of quota. The third review released SDR 23.333 million (about US$31.7 million), and the authorities committed to apply a safe harbour pricing formula for iron ore. It supports the public finances on which spending for the seven standards depends; debt remains at high risk of distress.

register.name: Sustainable Agricultural Value-chains Intensification for Growth (SAVIG)
register.note: Contributes to the Government’s goal of at least 35,000 formal jobs in agriculture
register.text: An IDA grant for production systems, post-harvest handling, processing and market links in priority agricultural value chains, with improved access to finance and digital agriculture solutions, for smallholder farmers, rural entrepreneurs and agribusiness operators. It serves the food and livelihood standards: 88.1% of Sierra Leoneans are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program, second operation (WARDIP2)
register.detail: World Bank Group · Approved 10 March 2026 · with Benin and Liberia
register.note: Sierra Leone’s share of the US$137 million operation (World Bank, Finances One)
register.text: Expands and upgrades digital infrastructure, fosters a more business-friendly environment and enables businesses to scale and operate across regional markets; about 5.2 million people in the three nations are to be connected to new or enhanced broadband. It serves the livelihood standard through jobs in an integrated regional digital market.

register.name: West Africa Food System Resilience Program, Phase 2, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 October 2025 · grant from the Least Developed Countries Fund of the Global Environment Facility
register.note: Scales up Phase 2 activities in Sierra Leone with nature-based solutions
register.text: An additional grant for integrated landscape management, biodiversity conservation and climate-sensitive interventions, with investments in research, innovation and community capacity building. It serves the food and livelihood standards, and the farmland and forest on this page.

register.name: Water Security and WASH Access Improvement Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 25 September 2025 · grant · first phase of a $180 million programme over the next decade
register.note: Approximately 5 million people expected to benefit
register.text: The first phase of a ten-year water, sanitation and hygiene programme: it improves the operational efficiency of the Guma Valley Water Company, expands toilets and hygiene in schools and health centres and adds fecal sludge treatment capacity. It serves water and shelter, where 10.9% of Sierra Leoneans have safely managed drinking water and 16.8% safely managed sanitation.

register.name: Macro Stability and Resilience Development Policy Operation, with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 13 December 2024 · $60 million grant as budget support · $20 million Cat DDO · first in a series of three
register.note: The $20 million Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option is contingent financing for the Government
register.text: Budget support for reforms to mobilize domestic revenue and enforce spending discipline, improve access to finance for the private sector by safeguarding financial sector stability, and enable private participation in the energy sector to improve the performance of the electricity utility, EDSA. It also supports climate and disaster resilience; it serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Enhancing Sierra Leone Energy Access
register.text: More homes, clinics and businesses connected to electricity.

register.name: Quality Essential Health Services and Systems Support Project
register.text: Essential care for mothers and children and a stronger health system.

register.name: Freetown WASH and Aquatic Environment Revamping Project
register.detail: IsDB · Endorsed at the 363rd meeting of the Board of Executive Directors · release of 13 December 2025
register.note: One of 14 operations approved for 12 member countries, US$1.365 billion in all
register.text: Improves water and sanitation services in Greater Freetown and restores key watershed areas. It serves the water standard, where 10.9% of Sierra Leoneans have safely managed drinking water, and the fresh water on this page.

register.name: Fostering Africa’s Agricultural Productivity through Fertilizer Value Chain Financing (FOSTER)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved 16 October 2025 · $1.5 million partial credit guarantee from the Africa Fertilizer Financing Mechanism · implemented by Welthungerhilfe
register.note: 9,500 metric tons of fertilizer for more than 126,000 farmers
register.text: A guarantee-led package that helps smallholder farmers obtain quality fertilizer through credit and guarantee schemes. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Livestock and Livelihoods Development Project
register.detail: IsDB · Signed 21 May 2025 in Algiers, at the 2025 IsDB Annual Meetings
register.note: Expected to boost agricultural productivity and food security in rural areas
register.text: An IsDB financing agreement for livestock and rural livelihoods. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Bumbuna-1 Hydroelectric Power Station Expansion
register.detail: OPEC Fund · Loan · 60 MW more renewable power for Freetown
register.text: Expands the nation’s main hydropower station to serve about 1.4 million people in the capital.

register.name: Salone Off-Grid Renewable Energy Acceleration (SOGREA)
register.detail: European Union and Denmark · implemented by UNOPS with SEforALL · launched 26 January 2026 · bidders workshop 10 and 11 June 2026
register.note: EUR 22 million of EU grants for private mini-grid developers, paid against verified milestones
register.text: A milestone-triggered partial reimbursement for private companies that finance, build, own and operate green mini-grids in rural Sierra Leone. By 2028 the EU funding is to bring over 31,000 new connections in at least 60 communities and about 5.2 megawatts of solar capacity. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Sierra Leone Compact
register.detail: Millennium Challenge Corporation · Signed 27 September 2024 · five-year grant · transmission, distribution and access, power sector reform
register.note: With a $14.2 million voluntary contribution from the Government of Sierra Leone
register.text: A five-year grant to expand the transmission network, make the grid more reliable and reduce losses and barriers to access, with a focus on schools, health facilities, businesses and households, and to reform the power sector to generate additional private financing. It aims to deliver affordable and reliable electricity for 4.6 million people; it serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Planting Naturals, sustainable organic palm oil
register.detail: AgDevCo · Announced 3 September 2025 · investment, with technical assistance
register.note: The company buys palm fruit from about 8,000 smallholder farmers and employs over 1,500 people
register.text: An investment by AgDevCo, a specialist impact investor in African agriculture, to increase fruit production and mill capacity and upgrade logistics, with technical assistance for farmer support programmes, including digital and traceability. It serves the livelihood standard in rural Sierra Leone.

register.name: Pee Cee Agriculture, onion farm
register.detail: IFC · Approved 30 September 2024 · signed 1 March 2025 · invested 7 April 2025 · project finance loan · Lungi, Port Loko District
register.note: Service agreements with 41 cooperatives, about 1,300 farmers, 80% of them women (2024)
register.text: A loan for a fully irrigated and mechanized 500-hectare farming operation to produce more than 40,000 tons of onions a year. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Rivers already give three quarters of the power; four in ten have electricity, and every new line can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 37.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Easy Solar
items.text: Sells solar power on pay-as-you-go terms, with customers paying in small amounts by mobile money, through an agent network that reaches remote communities across Sierra Leone and Liberia. Since 2016 it has delivered solar access to over one million people across West Africa.

items.name: Women in Energy Sierra Leone
items.text: A company that makes Smart Green Stoves for clean cooking and has produced over 3,500 of them; it has trained over 100 women, young people and persons with disabilities, and brought solar-powered cold rooms and smoking kilns to women fishmongers in Freetown.

items.name: Rising Academies
items.text: Founded in Sierra Leone in 2014, it improves learning for underserved children through curriculum materials, intensive teacher coaching and actionable data, and serves over 250,000 students across 700 schools in West and East Africa.

items.name: A Call to Business
items.text: A social enterprise that makes group and individual microloans, largely to informal entrepreneurs, with know-your-credit training; it collects savings at clients’ places of business through its Osusu account and runs a cashless agricultural lending model that supplies machinery and inputs. As of 30 December 2025 it served over 25,200 borrowers, 68 percent of them women.

items.name: Planting Naturals
items.text: A leading producer of sustainable organic palm oil that buys palm fruit from about 8,000 smallholder farmers in rural Sierra Leone and employs over 1,500 people; AgDevCo invested USD 7 million in September 2025.
